quizName: DMV Practice Test #3 20 Questions • Passing Score 15

questions.question: Before riding, check that:

options.text: The brakes make a loud squeaking noise.
The brakes rub against the steering.
Each brake can stop the motorcycle.
Only the rear brake can stop the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Each brake can stop the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Test each brake lever before you ride. Press each one fully and make sure it feels firm and stops the motorcycle.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT good clothing for riding?

options.text: A jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs.
Boots or shoes that cover your ankles.
A baseball cap for your hair.

questions.correctAnswerText: A baseball cap for your hair.
questions.explanation: To protect yourself, wear a DOT-approved helmet. Also wear face or eye protection, a sturdy jacket and long pants, boots or shoes that cover your ankles, and durable gloves.

questions.question: When it starts to rain, you should ride:

options.text: In any part of the lane.
Where car tires have left tracks.
In the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Where car tires have left tracks.
questions.explanation: Rain makes roads slippery. It is safest to ride where car tires have already marked the road.

questions.question: Which fabric protects motorcycle riders best?
questions.correctAnswerText: Leather.
questions.explanation: Leather jackets and pants offer the best protection for motorcycle riders.

questions.question: When choosing where to ride in a lane, think about:

options.text: Whether other drivers can see you.
Whether you can pass more vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Whether other drivers can see you.
questions.explanation: Choose a lane position that makes you visible to other drivers. Also make sure you have enough space around you.

questions.question: Common drugs like cold tablets:

options.text: Can affect your ability to ride safely.
Usually do not affect your riding ability.
Are safe and do not affect riding ability.
Are always safe before riding because you can buy them without a prescription.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can affect your ability to ride safely.
questions.explanation: Almost all drugs, even over-the-counter ones, can affect your ability to ride safely. Learn about side effects before taking any drug and riding.

questions.question: Taking corners too fast:

options.text: Can cause you to enter another lane.
Is better than going too slowly.
Usually keeps you in your lane.
Is okay because motorcycles are small.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can cause you to enter another lane.
questions.explanation: Taking a corner too fast may cause you to cross into another lane or leave the road. Slow down before you turn.

questions.question: For the most protection, use a helmet that:

options.text: Has been in a crash before.

questions.correctAnswerText: Meets U.S. DOT standards.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards. Your helmet should fit snugly all around your head.

questions.question: Intersections are usually:

options.text: Safe because there is lots of traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Dangerous for riders.
questions.explanation: Intersections are dangerous because many vehicles cross paths there. This creates the most risk for motorcycle riders.

questions.question: You should check your motorcycle:
questions.correctAnswerText: Before every ride.
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle before every ride. This takes just a few minutes and helps prevent problems before you get on the road.

questions.question: Do motorcycles have blind spots?

options.text: Yes, but they are so small they do not matter.
Yes, and you should check them regularly.
No, they are too small to have blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, and you should check them regularly.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like all vehicles. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes. Make head checks part of your regular scanning routine.

questions.question: What is the best gear to wear when riding?
questions.correctAnswerText: Gear that protects you.
questions.explanation: Wear gear that protects you while riding. Use a DOT-approved helmet, eye or face protection, and protective clothing.

questions.question: Which surface is NOT slippery?
questions.correctAnswerText: Dry concrete
questions.explanation: Many surfaces reduce tire grip. Wet pavement, gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, and metal plates are more dangerous for motorcycles than dry pavement.

questions.question: What color is a warning sign?
questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow with black lettering
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: What should you do before riding a motorcycle you have never used?

options.text: Test the seat to make sure it is comfortable.
Assume it is in good condition.
Practice the throttle, clutch, and brakes before riding.
Ride normally since most bikes are the same.

questions.correctAnswerText: Practice the throttle, clutch, and brakes before riding.
questions.explanation: Every motorcycle is different. Be careful when riding a new motorcycle. Learn how it works before you start. Practice using the throttle, clutch, and brakes to find the gear pattern.

questions.question: What is the most important thing you can do to survive a motorcycle accident?
questions.correctAnswerText: Wear a helmet.
questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet is the single most important way to reduce your risk of injury or death in an accident.

questions.question: What should you do when riding on a bridge grating?

options.text: Always stay on the right side of your lane.
Always stay on the left side of your lane.
Stay relaxed, keep a steady speed, and ride straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay relaxed, keep a steady speed, and ride straight.
questions.explanation: Bridge gratings may cause your motorcycle to weave. This is usually not dangerous. Relax and cross at a steady speed. Do not zigzag to fight the weave, as this is more dangerous and forces you out of your lane.

questions.question: What happens if you take a turn too fast on a motorcycle?

options.text: It is safe as long as you stay under the speed limit.
It is safer on a motorcycle than in a car.
It is safe if no other vehicles are near you.
You may slide into another lane or leave the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may slide into another lane or leave the road.
questions.explanation: Taking a turn too fast is dangerous. If you cannot hold the turn, you may slide into another lane or off the road. Always use caution when turning.

questions.question: What should you do if you feel tired while riding?

options.text: Keep riding and hope you wake up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest.
questions.explanation: Do not ride if you are tired. On long trips, take a rest break every two hours to avoid fatigue.

questions.question: What should you do when riding on a slippery surface?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, reduce your speed. Use both brakes when braking and avoid sudden movements.
